examples.en: He has a fiery temperament, so his voice is loud.
My grandmother has had a fiery personality since she was young.

examples.ko: 우리 이모는 말투가 괄괄하지만 마음은 따뜻해요.
examples.en: My aunt speaks bluntly and loudly, but she has a warm heart.
I like the way she laughs heartily.
The boss is straightforward and fiery.
If you have a fiery personality, people sometimes misunderstand you.

explain: 주로 사람의 성격이나 목소리가 거세고 활달할 때 써요. 같은 활발한 성격이라도 '시원시원하다'는 좋은 느낌이 강하고, '괄괄하다'는 거칠고 급한 느낌이 더 있어요. 주로 사람에게 쓰고, 칭찬보다는 성격을 묘사할 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for a person's temperament or voice that is strong, rough and lively. Even among energetic personalities, '시원시원하다' sounds more positive, while '괄괄하다' adds a rougher, hastier feel. It is used mainly for people, more to describe character than to praise.

examples.en: My friend nodded at what I said.
The teacher smiled and nodded.
I'm sleepy, so my head keeps nodding.

examples.ko: 고개를 끄덕거리며 이야기를 듣는 모습이 좋아요.
examples.en: I like how you listen to the story while nodding.
The child nods his head as if to say he understands.

examples.ko: 다들 고개를 끄덕거리지만 사실은 잘 모르는 것 같아요.
examples.en: Everyone is nodding, but they seem not to really understand.

explain: '끄덕이다'와 뜻이 거의 같지만 '-거리다'가 붙어서 고개를 여러 번 반복해서 움직이는 느낌이 있어요. 한 번 끄덕이는 동작은 '끄덕이다'가 자연스럽고, 보통 '고개를 끄덕거리다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It means almost the same as '끄덕이다', but the '-거리다' ending gives a feeling of repeating the movement several times. For a single nod, '끄덕이다' sounds more natural, and it is usually used as '고개를 끄덕거리다'.

en: show off; act pushy; butt in

examples.en: Why are you showing off so much?

examples.ko: 아무도 안 시켰는데 혼자 나대고 있어요.
examples.en: Nobody told him to, but he's busy butting in alone.
If you make a fuss over nothing, it's actually embarrassing.
My friend was showing off, and the mood got weird.
That kid tends to show off everywhere.
Don't push yourself forward so much, and stay quiet.

explain: 필요 없이 나서거나 잘난 척하며 설치는 사람에게 쓰는 부정적인 말투예요. 친구끼리 농담으로 쓰기도 하지만 윗사람이나 처음 만난 사람에게 쓰면 무례해요. 비슷한 말로 '설치다', '깝죽대다'가 있어요.
explain_en: A negative word for someone who pushes themselves forward or acts smug when it isn't needed. Friends may use it as a joke, but it is rude to elders or people you've just met. Similar words are 설치다 and 깝죽대다.

examples.en: When class ended, the students scattered in all directions.

examples.ko: 형편이 어려워서 가족들이 뿔뿔이 흩어져 살았대요.
examples.en: I heard the family was so badly off that they lived scattered apart.

examples.ko: 비가 오자 사람들이 뿔뿔이 집으로 돌아갔어요.
examples.en: When it started raining, people went their separate ways home.

examples.ko: 졸업하면 친구들이 뿔뿔이 다른 도시로 가요.
examples.en: After graduation, friends scatter off to different cities.
After the gathering ended, we split up and went our own ways.
The startled chickens ran off in every direction.

explain: 한곳에 있던 사람이나 동물이 각자 다른 방향으로 갈라질 때 써요. '흩어지다, 헤어지다, 도망가다' 같은 말과 자주 함께 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when people or animals that were together split off in different directions. It often appears with words like '흩어지다' (scatter), '헤어지다' (part) and '도망가다' (run away).

examples.en: That employee is a bit cold toward customers.
I'm sorry I answered so coldly.
His icy expression scared me at first.
She looks aloof, but she's actually very warm.
She turned away coldly and left.

examples.ko: 쌀쌀맞던 옆집 아저씨가 요즘은 먼저 인사해요.
examples.en: The neighbor who used to be so cold now greets me first.

explain: '쌀쌀하다'는 날씨에도 쓰지만 '쌀쌀맞다'는 사람의 태도나 말투에만 써요. 정이 없고 차갑게 대한다는 느낌이라 '냉정하다', '차갑다'와 비슷하지만 더 일상적인 말이에요.
explain_en: '쌀쌀하다' can describe weather, but '쌀쌀맞다' is only used for a person's attitude or tone. It means cold and unfriendly, similar to '냉정하다' or '차갑다' but more everyday.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 약아빠져서 자기 이익만 챙겨요.
examples.en: He is a sly operator who only looks out for his own interests.
Be careful not to be fooled by a crafty merchant.
I can't believe how cunning this little kid is.
He acted so calculating that his friends gradually drifted away.

examples.ko: 다들 약아빠졌다고 하지만 저한테는 늘 잘해 줘요.
examples.en: Everyone says he's sly, but he's always good to me.

examples.ko: 약아빠지지 않고 정직하게 사는 게 마음 편해요.
examples.en: Living honestly without being sly gives me peace of mind.

explain: '약삭빠르다'보다 거칠고 더 나쁘게 흉보는 말투예요. 자기 이익만 챙기는 약은 사람이나 행동을 말하고, 구어에서 많이 써요. 윗사람이나 격식 있는 자리에서는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: It is a rougher and more negative way to criticize than '약삭빠르다'. It describes a person or action that is crafty and only looks after its own benefit, and it is mostly spoken. It is best avoided with superiors or in formal settings.

en: double-dealing; speaking with a forked tongue; being double-tongued

examples.en: Going back on your word like that, you're someone who says one thing and does another.
When a politician goes back on their word, they lose people's trust.

examples.ko: 그는 약속해 놓고 일구이언해서 모두가 실망했어요.
examples.en: He made a promise and then went back on it, so everyone was disappointed.

examples.ko: 어제는 된다고 했다가 오늘은 안 된다니 일구이언 아니에요?
examples.en: You said yes yesterday and no today. Isn't that going back on your word?

examples.ko: 일구이언이라는 말을 들을까 봐 신중하게 대답했어요.
examples.en: I answered carefully so I wouldn't be called two-faced.

examples.ko: 일구이언하지 않는 사람이 결국 신뢰를 얻어요.
examples.en: People who don't go back on their word end up earning trust.

explain: '일구이언(을) 하다'나 '일구이언하다'로 써요. '말을 바꾸다'와 달리 신뢰를 어겼다는 비판이 강해서 가볍게 쓰면 꽤 센 말이 돼요.
explain_en: It is used as '일구이언(을) 하다' or '일구이언하다'. Unlike '말을 바꾸다' (to change one's words), it carries strong criticism for breaking trust, so using it casually sounds quite harsh.

en: creator; author of an original work

examples.ko: 이 웹툰의 창작자는 아직 스무 살이에요.
examples.en: The creator of this webtoon is still twenty years old.

examples.ko: 창작자와 직접 이야기할 수 있는 행사가 있어요.
examples.en: There is an event where you can talk directly with the creator.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 창작자가 되고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I have wanted to become a creator since I was little.

examples.ko: 좋은 창작자는 매일 조금씩 작품을 만들어요.
examples.en: A good creator makes a little work every day.

examples.ko: 창작자의 허락 없이 그림을 쓰면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not use a drawing without the creator's permission.
There are so many young creators on the internet.

explain: 창작자는 만든 사람 중에서도 처음부터 새로 만든 사람을 가리켜요. 그림, 노래, 글처럼 작품을 만드는 사람에게 쓰고, 공장에서 물건을 만드는 사람에게는 '제작자'나 '생산자'를 써요. 요즘은 유튜브나 웹툰에서 활동하는 사람을 말할 때 자주 들려요.
explain_en: 창작자 is someone who makes an original work from scratch, like a drawing, song, or story. For people who produce goods in a factory, Koreans say 제작자 or 생산자 instead. You hear it a lot now for people active on YouTube or in webtoons.
